claims.text: The starting material is bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Bulk HfNbTaTiZr has low thermal conductivity.
The low thermal conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr is desirable for thermal insulation.
Adding elements with different atomic radii will introduce a controlled amount of lattice distortion into HfNbTaTiZr.
The intervention will produce lattice disorder in addition to lattice distortion.
Lattice distortions and defects scatter phonons.
The increased phonon scattering will reduce the phonon mean free path.
Reducing the phonon mean free path will reduce phonon thermal conductivity.
The alloyed material will have lower phonon thermal conductivity than the unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr baseline.
The prediction applies from nearly 0 to 200 K and from 300 to 1200 K.
Bulk HfNbTaTiZr without the additional alloying intervention is the comparison baseline.
The magnitude of the effect depends on temperature and composition ranges in which the alloying effect is significant.
The required amount of lattice distortion and the optimal alloying elements are uncertain.
Failure of different-radius alloying to reduce phonon thermal conductivity would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as HfNbTaTiZr 'without alloying,' even though HfNbTaTiZr is itself a multicomponent alloy. The intended distinction appears to be without additional alloying, but the wording is internally inconsistent.
